name: Rorathang
tagline: River junction where the Silk Route road turns
meta_description: Rorathang, Sikkim: riverside town at about 500 m where the Rangpo meets the Pachey and Reshi, and the road to Rongli and Rhenock branches off. Fares and tips.
summary: Rorathang is a riverside town at about 500 m on NH717A in Pakyong district, where the Rangpo river meets the Pachey and Reshi streams. Roads branch here to Rongli, Rhenock, Pakyong and Rangpo. For most travellers it is a tea stop on the way to Aritar or the Silk Route, and a transport junction.
intro: Rorathang lies on the bank of the Rangpo river on National Highway 717A, about 12 km from Rangpo, 9 km from Rhenock, 14 km from Rongli and 19 km from Pakyong, according to Wikipedia. It sits in a river valley and is a busy small town, with industrial units in the area, including several pharmaceutical plants.

Roads join here from Rangpo through Kumrek, from Pakyong via Tareythang and Taza, and from Rongli via Mulukay. Wikipedia says taxi and jeep services run from Rorathang to Gangtok, Pakyong, Rhenock, Singtam, Rangpo, Rongli, Ranipool and Siliguri, with SNT buses on several routes. It is the practical transport junction for the lower Silk Route.

Few visitors sleep here. They stop for tea and momos, change vehicles or buy supplies. Pakyong Airport is about 11 km away by Wikipedia's figure, but there have been no scheduled flights since June 2024, so plan on Bagdogra (IXB) or NJP. Check current status of roads before you travel.

story.title: Where three rivers meet
story.text: Wikipedia's article on Rorathang says the confluence of the Rangpo river with its tributaries, the Pachey and the Reshi, is at Rorathang. After the Rangpo meets the Reshi, it also marks the boundary between Sikkim and West Bengal, and villages of Kalimpong district can be reached from Rorathang after crossing the Reshi. The same article lists roads that join NH 717A here, which is why the town works as a junction. The Rangpo then runs on to Rangpo town and the Teesta. The article also says the town and surroundings are an important industrial hub of Sikkim, hosting several pharmaceutical companies, which explains the trucks and workers' buses on the road. For a traveller, the story is simple: this is where the valleys gather and the roads divide, one to the Silk Route, one to Aritar, one to Gangtok.

little_known.fact: Wikipedia says the Rangpo river meets its tributaries, the Pachey and the Reshi, at Rorathang, and that the river marks part of the Sikkim and West Bengal boundary after meeting the Reshi.
Four roads join NH717A at Rorathang, according to Wikipedia: from Rangpo via Kumrek, from Pakyong via Tareythang, from Rongli via Mulukay and from Pakyong via Taza.

Wikipedia lists the nearest working railway stations to Rorathang as Sevoke Junction about 65 km, Siliguri Junction about 86 km and New Jalpaiguri about 92 km. The Rangpo station is under construction.

facts: River junction, road hub, industrial area

highlights.title: A junction for the lower Silk Route
highlights.text: Roads branch here to Rongli, Rhenock, Pakyong and Rangpo. Drivers stop for tea, and shared jeeps change here. Know which turning your driver is taking.

highlights.title: River confluence
highlights.text: The Rangpo meets the Pachey and Reshi streams here. View from a safe bank or bridge, never at the edge, and avoid it after heavy rain.

highlights.title: Tea and momo stop
highlights.text: Small stalls serve tea, momos and noodles, at about ₹100–250. A good stop to stretch your legs on the 2 hour drive.

highlights.title: Supplies
highlights.text: Shops sell water, snacks and basics. Withdraw cash at Rangpo, Pakyong or Rhenock because ATM availability in Rorathang may vary.

highlights.title: Gateway to Kalimpong district villages
highlights.text: Wikipedia says villages across the Reshi can be reached from Rorathang. Ask locally before crossing, and carry ID.

how_to_reach.text: Shared jeeps and SNT buses run from Gangtok via Pakyong, Rangpo and Rongli, taking about 2 hours from Gangtok, at roughly ₹150–300 a seat. Many Rongli and Rhenock jeeps pause here. Check current status before you travel.

From Gangtok about 50 km and 2 hours via Ranipool and Pakyong, or via NH10 and Rangpo. A reserved small car costs about ₹3,000–4,000 one way. NH10 can close in the monsoon after slides; the alternative is via Kalimpong.

About 98 km from Bagdogra and 92 km from NJP by Wikipedia's figures, taking about 3.5 to 4 hours via Sevoke and Rangpo. Pakyong Airport has no scheduled flights since June 2024. Plan on Bagdogra (IXB) or NJP.

costs: Reserved small car Gangtok to Rorathang
where_to_stay: Rorathang has a few small lodges for business travellers at roughly ₹1,000–2,000 a room, though we do not name them. Most visitors sleep at Aritar, 20 km or so away, in lakeside homestays, or at Pakyong, where Vivanta Sikkim is the comfort option. For the Silk Route, Lingtam or Padamchen with a permit from Rongli are the usual choices. Ask us if you need a late-night stop near the junction.
tips: Know which road your driver is taking at the junction: Rongli, Rhenock or Pakyong.
Stop for tea here and stretch your legs; the hill roads are winding.
Carry cash; withdraw at Rangpo or Pakyong.
Stay away from the river in or after heavy rain.
Check current status of NH10 and the Rongli road before you travel.

experiences.title: Junction tea and momo stop
experiences.summary: A deliberate stop at the junction: milk tea, a plate of momos and a look at the traffic on the way to Rongli, Rhenock or Pakyong.
body: Rorathang's tea stalls serve drivers, factory workers and travellers. Order milk tea and a plate of momos and watch the junction: trucks, jeeps, school buses and shared taxis all pass through.
Ask your driver about the roads that branch here. Wikipedia lists four joining roads: from Rangpo, Pakyong (two ways) and Rongli. It helps to know which one you are on.
Carry sanitiser and water. Eat where it is busy. If you have a long drive ahead, eat lightly.

faqs.q: Are there vegetarian options?
faqs.a: Yes, vegetable momos, noodles and fried snacks are common. Say if you avoid onion, garlic or egg.

faqs.q: Is there an ATM?
faqs.a: ATM availability may vary. Withdraw cash at Rangpo, Pakyong or Rhenock before you rely on it.

faqs.q: How long should we stop?
faqs.a: About 30 to 45 minutes is enough for tea and a short walk.

experiences.title: Three rivers bridge view
experiences.summary: A short stop at a bridge or bank to see where the Rangpo meets the Pachey and Reshi and to read the border river's geography.
body: Wikipedia says the Rangpo meets its tributaries, the Pachey and the Reshi, at Rorathang, and that the river marks part of the boundary between Sikkim and West Bengal after meeting the Reshi.
Ask your driver or a local to point out safe viewpoints near a bridge. Stand back from the edge, and avoid the stop in or after rain.
Early morning gives clear light and fewer vehicles. Look for wagtails and dippers on rocks. Do not swim and keep children away from the bank.

faqs.q: Which rivers meet at Rorathang?
faqs.a: Wikipedia says the Rangpo meets the Pachey and Reshi at Rorathang.

faqs.q: Is the river the state border?
faqs.a: Wikipedia says the Rangpo marks part of the Sikkim and West Bengal boundary after meeting the Reshi.

faqs.q: Is it safe to go close?
faqs.a: No. Stay on the bank or bridge. Water rises quickly after rain.

experiences.title: Kali Khola falls roadside stop
experiences.best_time: Jul–Oct for flow; visit only in settled weather
experiences.summary: A roadside stop at the waterfall Wikipedia lists as Kali Khola falls (also called Lonely falls) on the Rorathang to Rongli road, when conditions allow.
body: Wikipedia's Aritar article lists Kali Khola falls, about 100 m high, on the Rorathang to Rongli road. We have not verified the exact stopping place, so ask your driver where it is safe to pull over.
Flow is strongest in and after the monsoon, which is also the riskiest time for slides. Visit in settled weather only, and never stand under or near the base after heavy rain.
Keep to the road side and do not clamber on wet rocks. Take photographs from a safe distance and take your litter with you.

faqs.q: Where exactly are Kali Khola falls?
faqs.a: Wikipedia places them on the Rorathang to Rongli road. Ask your driver for the safe pull-off.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see them?
faqs.a: After rain, flow is strongest, but slides are also more likely. Early autumn is a good compromise. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is it safe to go close?
faqs.a: No. Stay at a distance and away from loose slopes.

experiences.title: Rangpo valley road drive
experiences.summary: A drive along the Rangpo valley between Rangpo and Rorathang, with river views, small farms and the industrial belt that sits oddly beside paddy terraces.
body: Wikipedia says Rorathang and nearby areas host several pharmaceutical factories, which makes this valley one of Sikkim's industrial hubs. The contrast with paddy terraces and farm villages is striking.
The road between Rangpo and Rorathang follows the river about 12 km. Stop for tea and photographs only where drivers know it is safe.
Do not photograph factory gates or workers. Expect trucks and workers' buses. In the monsoon, check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Rangpo from Rorathang?
faqs.a: About 12 km by Wikipedia's figure, taking about 30 to 45 minutes.

faqs.q: Are factories open to visitors?
faqs.a: No. Do not photograph gates or workers.

faqs.q: Is the road safe?
faqs.a: Usually, but slides can follow heavy rain. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is Rorathang known for?
faqs.a: Rorathang is known as a river-junction town and road hub at about 500 m, where roads to Rongli, Rhenock, Pakyong and Rangpo meet, and where the Rangpo meets the Pachey and Reshi.

faqs.q: How far is Rorathang from Gangtok?
faqs.a: About 50 km, taking about 2 hours via Pakyong. Landslides can add time. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Rorathang worth a stop?
faqs.a: For tea and a river view, yes. It is not a sightseeing town.

faqs.q: Do we need a permit for Rorathang?
faqs.a: No. Rorathang is outside the Silk Route protected area. The permit starts at Rongli, for Indian nationals only. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Rorathang from Rongli?
faqs.a: About 14 km, taking about 45 minutes on a winding road.

faqs.q: How far is Rorathang from Aritar?
faqs.a: About 20 km by hill road, taking about an hour, via Rhenock. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there a hotel in Rorathang?
faqs.a: A few small lodges exist at about ₹1,000–2,000 a room. Most travellers stay at Aritar, Pakyong or Rongli area.

faqs.q: Is Pakyong Airport near Rorathang?
faqs.a: About 11 km by Wikipedia's figure, but there are no scheduled flights since June 2024. Plan on Bagdogra (IXB) or NJP.

faqs.q: What is the best time to pass through?
faqs.a: October to March for clear weather. The monsoon brings slides, and the rivers rise fast.
